\subsubsection{Monte Carlo and Yield}\label{sss:pixtop-mc}

200 samples of process and mismatch together, at the nominal process point and
\SI{37}{\celsius}, on the tapeout cell itself: the statistical model section
resolves \num{1070} random variables and all 200 samples converge.
Table~\ref{tab:pixtop-mc} is the result, and it is the first yield statement
this channel has. It is not visible from the corner runs of
Section~\ref{sss:pixtop-power}, where every dc specification passes at all five
corners: uncalibrated per-channel yield here is \SI{0.50}{\percent}.

Mismatch is the whole of it. A process-only run leaves \SI{0.68}{\percent} of
\(\sigma\) on the zero-current output --- \SI{0.005}{\percent} of the variance
--- and under \SI{1.5}{\percent} on every other quantity, and the two runs add
in quadrature to the combined \(\sigma\) within \SI{0.4}{\percent}. Six further
mismatch-only runs, each suppressing one matched structure, locate it: the
transimpedance amplifier A2 alone sets the current axis, taking \(\sigma\) of
the zero-current output from \num{5.759} to \SI{0.034}{\milli\volt} when it is
suppressed, and the control amplifier A1 alone sets the potential axis,
\num{5.559} to \SI{0.042}{\milli\volt}. The two R-2R ladders move only the
common mode and the DAC gain, both of which pass 200/200; the 320-code feedback
ladder and the local bias generator move no dc quantity by more than the
sampling error of a 100-sample run. The feedback ladder cannot enter: the
readout is \(V_{\mathrm{CM}} - I R_f\), so \(R_f\) is a gain a constant
multiplies out while the two amplifiers are a raw additive input offset. The
same offset is what the flat bench of Section~\ref{ss:pixel} measured
mismatch-only at \SI{5.72}{\milli\volt}; the assembled channel with process
\emph{and} mismatch reproduces it at \SIrange{5.55}{5.75}{\milli\volt}, so
assembly and process add nothing.

Because the die-common term is that small, the four channels are very nearly
independent and the four-channel figures below are per-channel yield to the
fourth power.

The zero-current output is gain-independent \emph{per sample}. Its mean and
\(\sigma\) agree to five significant figures at \(N = 0\), 63 and 319, and
within one sample the three taps agree to a few microvolts. One stored constant
therefore calibrates all 320 gain codes on a real channel, not only at the
typical point where Section~\ref{sss:pixtop-zero} measured it --- the premise
the whole current-axis calibration rests on.

\paragraph{The tracking specification is the working window.} The
\SI{2}{\milli\volt} reference-tracking limit is specified over the
\SIrange{0.4}{2.1}{\volt} commanded range, not over the full
\SIrange{0}{2.42}{\volt} code sweep. Inside that window the tracking error is a
pure constant per channel: after the mid-code value is removed the residual is
\SI{0.36}{\milli\volt} at \SI{0.63}{\volt} and falls further toward mid-code
(Figure~\ref{fig:pixtop-mc}). Outside it A1's input pair is running out of
common-mode range, the error stops being a constant, and the same residual is
\SI{3.5}{\milli\volt} at \SI{0.31}{\volt} --- which no stored constant reaches.
On the same samples and the same calibration the worst tracking error averages
\SI{0.873}{\milli\volt} over the window and \SI{5.841}{\milli\volt} over the
full sweep, and that specification alone yields \SI{96.5}{\percent} against
\SI{9.0}{\percent}. The difference is a choice of range, not a circuit
difference, and the electrochemistry does not use the outermost
\SI{0.4}{\volt} at the bottom or \SI{0.32}{\volt} at the top.

Stability is the one axis that needs nothing. A separate 200-sample run at the
worst electrode-by-gain point of Section~\ref{sss:pixtop-stability} passes
200/200, with \SI{74.11}{\degree} of transimpedance phase margin,
\(\sigma = \SI{3.07}{\degree}\) and a worst sample of \SI{64.35}{\degree} ---
\num{9.5} standard deviations above the \SI{45}{\degree} limit. Gain margins
are \(21.57 \pm \SI{0.88}{\decibel}\) and \(38.17 \pm \SI{0.64}{\decibel}\).
The compensation capacitor is not a marginal fix that mismatch undoes.

\paragraph{Yield.} Uncalibrated, \SI{0.50}{\percent} of channels meet all
twenty specifications and \SI{0.0000}{\percent} of four-channel chips do. The
two constants of Section~\ref{ss:calibration}, each measured through the
channel's own converter and so carrying that path's \SI{0.65}{\milli\volt} rms
floor, take the zero-current and gain-code specifications to \SI{100}{\percent}
each and per-channel yield to \SI{9.00}{\percent}, or \SI{0.0066}{\percent}
over four. Scoring the tracking specification over its working window instead
of the full sweep takes the same calibrated samples to \SI{61.50}{\percent} per
channel and \SI{14.31}{\percent} over four. What binds there is the
reference-electrode floor at \SI{65.5}{\percent}, which is the same offset seen
from the other side: the electrode cannot be driven below ground, so the floor
is A1's offset rectified at zero commanded potential and about a third of
samples exceed \SI{5}{\milli\volt}.

\textbf{Every yield above is an upper bound.} Four devices in the amplifier ---
two n-channel and two p-channel, in the enable and class-AB bias network ---
instantiate raw model cards instead of the mismatch-enabled wrappers, so they
drew no mismatch (Section~\ref{sss:pixtop-open}). The amplifiers are what set
every distribution in Table~\ref{tab:pixtop-mc}, and four more mismatching
devices in each can only widen the spread. The calibration the good numbers
assume is also not executable on this cell: it is measured through the
common-mode multiplexer slot, which collapses the channel it is calibrating
until that tap is buffered (Section~\ref{sss:pixtop-open}).
